rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the clause as disconnected from the preceding one: God does not command people to take angels and prophets as lords.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه 80 فجاءت منقطعة من الأول

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash instead reads the clause circumstantially, ‘while He does not command you.’
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش أي وهو لا يأمركم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وأهل الحرمين
rows.claim: Abu Amr, al-Kisai, and the people of the two sanctuaries read according to al-Akhfash’s construal.
rows.anchor: وهذه قراءة أبي عمرو والكسائي وأهل الحرمين

rows.speaker: اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls al-Yazidi’s report that Abu Amr made the rāʾ quiescent an error.
rows.anchor: رواية اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو أنه أسكن الراء فغلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the phrase in coordination with the preceding statement that no human would command this after receiving scripture.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه وقرأ بعضهم ( ولا يأمركم ) على قوله

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وحمزة وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq, Hamza, and Asim read the construction in the subjunctive, meaning ‘that you take angels and prophets as lords.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر النصب قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق وحمزة وعاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Christians exalt angels and prophets until treating them as lords.
rows.anchor: وهذا موجود في النصارى يعظمون الملائكة والأنبياء

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians are said to report a saying from Solomon telling one lord to sit at his right hand, which they apply to God addressing Christ.
rows.anchor: ويروون عن سليمان صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال ربي لربي

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains mā as a relative pronoun, ‘that which.’
rows.anchor: سألت الخليل في قوله جل وعز وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين فقال ما بمعنى الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On al-Khalil’s analysis, the pronoun after ātaytukum is omitted after a long phrase; al-ladhī is subject, min identifies the kind of gift, and the following phrase is its predicate.
rows.anchor: التقدير على قول الخليل للذي آتيتكموه ثم حذف الهاء لطول الاسم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats mā as extra and allows the promise to believe in the messenger as the predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش هي زائدة ويجوز أن يكون الخبر

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai takes mā conditionally and parses it as the object of ātaytukum.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي ما للشرط فعلى قوله موضعها نصب بآتيتكم

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read lammā with kasra on the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة ( لما آتيتكم ) بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ understands the covenant as being taken for the scripture and wisdom given to the prophets; the promise to believe is part of taking that covenant.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء أي أخذ الميثاق للذي آتاهم من كتاب وحكمة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the People of Scripture were pledged to believe in the messenger mentioned in the Torah.
rows.anchor: ولأبي عبيدة في هذا قول حسن قال المعنى وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view supplies omitted wording: the prophets were pledged to teach scripture and wisdom and to take people’s pledge to believe; the later reference to the pledge signals the ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقيل في الكلام حذف والمعنى وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is conditional: whoever turns away from belief after the covenant receives the answer that such people are rebellious.
rows.anchor: شرط والمعنى فمن تولى عن الإيمان بعد أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayra is the object of yabghūn.
rows.anchor: نصبت غير يبتغون ( وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm may optionally assimilate into the following mīm.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت أدغمت الميم في الميم وقد ذكرنا

words: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of two explanations, he gives ‘submitted and humbled’ first: all creatures are subject to God’s will, in conditions they welcome or dislike.
rows.anchor: أولهما أن يكون المعنى وله خضع وذل من في السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The healthy submit willingly and gladly, while the sick are subdued even when unwilling.
rows.anchor: فالصحيح منقاد طايع محب لذلك والمريض منقاد خاضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawʿan and karhan are verbal nouns used circumstantially, meaning ‘willingly’ and ‘under compulsion.’
rows.anchor: و ( طوعا وكرها ) مصدر في موضع الحال أي طايعين مكرهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains the religion’s rules, including what is lawful and forbidden.
rows.anchor: أي ليبين لكم أمر دينكم وما يحل لكم وما يحرم عليكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabic uses lām in place of an with verbs of wanting or commanding because both take a future action.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء العرب تأتي باللام على معنى كي في موضع أن

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq rejects treating lām as equivalent to an: on that analysis another lām would enter, as in ‘I came in order to honor you.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق وهذا خطأ ولو كانت اللام بمعنى أن لدخلت عليها لام أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq cites an anonymous line using لكيما as evidence for the lām construction.
rows.anchor: أردت لكيما يعلم الناس أنها … سراويل قيس والوفود شهود

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq parses the meaning as ‘He wanted this in order to make matters clear to you.’
rows.anchor: والتقدير أراد به ليبين لكم قال أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers call this the lām of an; another explanation is that God wants this for the sake of explaining, as in ‘I was commanded to act justly.’
rows.anchor: حتى سماها بعض القراء لام أن وقيل المعنى يريد الله هذا

rows.speaker: بعض أهل النظر
rows.claim: Some scholars infer that everything forbidden here was also forbidden to earlier communities.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل النظر في هذا دليل على أن كل ما حرم قبل هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar rejects that inference: the verse may explain earlier people who avoided prohibitions or how God guided earlier prophets without asserting identical rules.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا غلط لأنه قد يكون المعنى ويبين لكم أمر من قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause begins a new subject-predicate statement, and an is governed in the accusative by yurīdu.
rows.anchor: 27 ابتداء وخبر وأن في موضع نصب بيريد وكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuliqa is passive, and ḍaʿīfan is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ( وخلق الإنسان ) اسم ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Desire, appetite, and anger easily sway people; this weakness makes divine concessions necessary.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن هواه يستميله وشهوته وغضبه يستخفانه وهذا أشد الضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongful consumption includes gambling and every other prohibited way of taking property.
rows.anchor: أي بالظلم ويدخل في هذا القمار وكل ما نهي عنه

words: إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم
rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The people of Medina and Abu Amr read tijāratun in the nominative.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأبي عمرو

words: إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم
rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: The Kufans read tijāratan in the accusative, which Abu Ubayd prefers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ( تجارة ) بالنصب وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar considers the accusative remote in meaning and grammar: this consensual trade is not wrongful consumption, and the exception construction calls for the nominative.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر النصب بعيد من جهة المعنى والإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is an accusative exception, not an exception from the prior category; kāna means ‘occur,’ a usage normally followed by the nominative.
rows.anchor: لأن أن ههنا في موضع نصب لأنها استثناء ليس من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a prohibition against killing yourselves.
rows.anchor: ( ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم ) نهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy is shown by forbidding people to harm one another.
rows.anchor: أي فبرحمته نهاكم عن هذا ومنع بعضكم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is accusative and means ‘in shortening.’ Abu Ubayda lists three forms for shortening prayer: qaṣartu, qaṣṣartu, and aqṣartu.
rows.anchor: أن في موضع نصب أي في أن تقصروا قال أبو عبيدة فيها ثلاث لغات

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the Hijazis use fatantu; Tamim, Rabiʿa, Qays, Asad, and other Najdis use aftantu.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء أهل الحجاز يقولون فتنت الرجل وتميم وربيعة وقيس وأسد

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh distinguish the forms: fatantu puts someone to trial, while aftantu makes someone afflicted by trial.
rows.anchor: وفرق الخليل وسيبويه بينهما فقالا فتنتة جعلت فيه فتنة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says he does not recognize aftantuhu with an initial alif.
rows.anchor: وزعم الأصمعي أنه لا يعرف أفتنته بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form has kasra on the imperative lām; it is dropped because it is heavy.
rows.anchor: والأصل فلتقم حذفت الكسرة لثقلها

rows.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Kisai, and al-Farrāʾ report that imperative, purpose, and negative lām can take fatḥa.
rows.anchor: حكى الأخفش والكسائي والفراء أن لام الأمر ولام كي ولام الجحود يفتحن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh rejects opening this lām because it would erase the distinction between the prepositional lām and emphatic lām.
rows.anchor: وسيبويه يمنع من هذا لعلة موجبة وهي الفرق بين لام الجر ولام التوكيد

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the report is not accepted from an isolated source against early grammarians; even a sincere informant could have heard incorrectly.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق لا يلتفت إلى حكاية حاك لم يروها النحويون القدماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same lām analysis applies to taking weapons and the following commands to stand behind and for another group to pray.
rows.anchor: وكذا ( وليأخذوا أسلحتهم ) وكذا

words: ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘no blame’ clause is nominative; an taḍaʿū is accusative as the object of placing the weapons down.
rows.anchor: ( ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى ) في موضع رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief entry labels the relevant expression in verse 103 a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: 103 حال 104 نهي وقرأ عبد الرحمن

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن الأعرج
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman al-Aʿraj reads an with fatḥa, meaning ‘because you suffer.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن الأعرج ( أن تكونوا تألمون ) بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: منصور بن المعتمر
rows.claim: Mansur ibn al-Muʿtamir reads the tāʾ in taʾlamūn with kasra to show the active form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ منصور بن المعتمر ( إن تكونوا تيلمون ) بكسر التاء

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians disallow kasra on the tāʾ because the resulting kasra sequence is too heavy.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز عند البصريين في تألمون كسر التاء لثقل الكسر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām expresses purpose.
rows.anchor: لام كي وروي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو أنهما أدغما الميم

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Amr are reported to assimilate mīm into bāʾ, though grammarians disallow it because mīm is nasalized.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو أنهما أدغما الميم في الباء ولا يجيز ذلك النحويون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is conditional, the next phrase is coordinated with it, and Sibawayh’s analysis supplies omitted wording at the beginning.
rows.anchor: 112 شرط ( ثم يرم به ) عطف عليه وفي الكلام حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats khatiʾa and ithm as synonyms whose different wording permits coordination; another makes khatiʾa a minor sin and ithm a major one.
rows.anchor: أجوبة منها أنهما واحد ولكن لما اختلف اللفظان جاز هذا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says God calls some sins khatiʾa and others ithm; imputing either to an innocent person is slander and a manifest sin.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق سمى الله جل وعز بعض المعاصي خطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buhtān is a lie so outrageous that its magnitude leaves people astonished.
rows.anchor: والبهتان الكذب الذي يتحير من عظمه وشأنه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: For Sibawayh, the phrase after lawlā is a subject with an unexpressed predicate.
rows.anchor: ما بعد لولا مرفوع بالابتداء عند سيبويه والخبر محذوف لا يظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor and mercy mean that He alerted the Prophet to the truth.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته بأن نبهك على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group tried to mislead the Prophet after asking him to clear Ibn Ubayriq and shift the accusation to a Jew; God instead made the truth clear.
rows.anchor: لأنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يبرىء ابن أبيرق من التهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They only mislead themselves by acting like the misguided, while God protects His Messenger.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين والله جل وعز يعصم رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet because he is protected.
rows.anchor: ( وما يضرونك من شيء ) لأنك معصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn’s ḍamma is omitted for jussive mood, wāw drops when quiescent letters meet, and taʿlamu is the predicate of takun.
rows.anchor: حذفت الضمة من النون للجزم وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwā can mean private conversation or the matter people privately urge one another to pursue.
rows.anchor: نجواهم في العربية على معنيين أحدهما أنه يكون لما يتناجون به

words: إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the conversation sense, min is an accusative exception outside the original category: there is good in urging charity, right conduct, or reconciliation.
rows.anchor: فمن في موضع نصب لأنه استثناء ليس من الأول أي لكن من أمر بصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively min is genitive, with the sense ‘except in the private conversation of one who urges charity.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من في موضع خفض ويكون التقدير إلا في نجوى من أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwā can also mean the group conferring; min is then genitive as an appositive or accusative by another exception construction.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الآخر أن النجوى تكون الجماعة المفردين فيكون من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from stripping something away and isolating it; najwa also names raised ground standing apart from its surroundings.
rows.anchor: ونجوى مشتقة من نجوت الشيء أنجوه أي خلصته وأفردته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poem compares someone on a raised patch with someone at its edge, witnessing the word for elevated ground.
rows.anchor: فمن بنجوته كمن بعقوته … والمستكن كمن يمشي بقرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is conditional; ibtighāʾa is a purpose complement and the answer promises a great reward.
rows.anchor: ( ومن يفعل ذلك ) شرط ( ابتغاء مرضاة الله ) مفعول من أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ’s ḍamma is omitted for heaviness, though the original form may be kept in poetry.
rows.anchor: حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها ويجوز أن يؤتى به على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is jussive as a conditional; the doubled qāf appears because the second falls where a quiescent letter would, and kasra separates two quiescents.
rows.anchor: 115 جزم لأنه شرط وظهر التضعيف لأن القاف الثانية في موضع سكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the conditional response; the final yāʾ may be dropped with its kasra retained, or the wāw restored with ḍamma, or the wāw dropped.
rows.anchor: قوله ( نوله ما تولى ) جواب الشرط وإن شئت حذفت الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects making the hāʾ quiescent because it is too weakly articulated; the phrase is an accusative explanatory specification.
rows.anchor: فأما إسكان الهاء فلا يجوز لخفائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbārīn is an adjective, while the predicate of inna is in the prepositional phrase; ḥattā takes the future subjunctive.
rows.anchor: 22 اسم إن ( جبارين ) نعت والخبر في الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may assimilate into rāʾ, and the jīm in rajulayni may be quiescent because its ḍamma is heavy.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الإدغام إدغام اللام في الراء ويجوز إسكان الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With yāʾ kasra, the two men are tyrants favored by God with Islam; with yāʾ fatḥa, they are Moses’s people who fear the tyrants, though they could themselves be tyrants.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ ( يخافون ) قال هما جباران من الله عليهما بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overt subject is coordinated with the pronoun after emphasis. Basrans find this poor without emphasis, though poetry permits it; al-Farrāʾ permits it everywhere.
rows.anchor: ( فاذهب أنت وربك ) عطف على المضمر الذي في فاذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʿidūn is the predicate of inna; in non-Quranic usage qāʿidīn could be circumstantial because the sentence is complete.
rows.anchor: ( إنا ههنا قاعدون ) خبر إن ويجوز في غير القرآن

words: إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is dropped to avoid three consecutive nūns; akhī may be accusative with nafsī or the noun of inna, or nominative by position or coordination with the hidden pronoun.
rows.anchor: الأصل إنني حذفت النون لاجتماع النونات ( وأخي ) في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna transmits that ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read fa-friq with kasra on rāʾ, meaning ‘separate us’ by assigning the believers Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير أنه قرأ ( فافرق ) بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land is forbidden in the sense that they are barred from entering it, as in the idiom ‘May God forbid your face from the Fire.’
rows.anchor: ومعنى محرمة أنهم ممنوعون من دخولها كما يقال حرم الله وجهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an adverb of time.
rows.anchor: حرم الله وجهك على النار ( أربعين سنة ) ظرف زمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is imperative; its wāw is dropped.
rows.anchor: أمر فلذلك حذفت منه الواو أمر الله تعالى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to recount the story to the Jews to answer their rejection of him; it shows they are no more honored than Adam’s sons and supports Muhammad’s prophethood because he had not read books.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يتلو على اليهود خبر ابني آدم

rows.speaker: عمرو ومجاهد
rows.claim: Amr and Mujahid say the offerers were Israelites; Abu Jaʿfar rejects this because the next verse says the killer was shown how to bury his brother.
rows.anchor: وأما قول عمرو مجاهد إن اللذين قربا قربانا من بني إسرائيل فغلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious from whom God accepts offerings are those who avoid sins.
rows.anchor: أي من المتقين من المعاصي

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid takes the believer’s wanting figuratively: since he wants reward and does not reach out to kill, he is treated as if he wanted the outcome.
rows.anchor: محمد بن يزيد هذا مجاز لما كان المؤمن يريد الثواب ولا يبسط يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the wish literally: the would-be killer has earned Hell by threatening murder, so the believer should wish he be among its people.
rows.anchor: والجواب الآخر أنه حقيقة لأنه لما قال له لأقتلنك استوجب النار

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s preferred interpretation is ‘with our two sins’: verbal nouns can attach to their agent or object, as in ‘the property between me and you’ meaning between us.
rows.anchor: فمن أحسن ما قيل فيه وهو مذهب سيبويه أن المعنى بإثمنا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh cites ‘which of me and you was worse?’ to show paired first- and second-person forms can mean ‘which of us.’
rows.anchor: وأنشد ( فأيي ما وأيك كان شرا ) أي فأينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take the phrase as the sin of the threat, or the sin of killing the speaker if the threat is carried out.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بإثمي بإثم قولك لي لأقتلنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated; ‘that is the recompense of wrongdoers’ is a subject-predicate sentence.
rows.anchor: ( فتكون من أصحاب النار ) عطف ( وذلك جزاء الظالمين ) ابتداء وخبر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar calls the preceding explanation far-fetched, since ordinary Arabic says ‘his soul complied with him.’
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر هذا بعيد لأنه إنما يقال طاوعته نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul made the killing desirable to him.
rows.anchor: أي أحدث له شهوة في هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is purposive as events culminate in this outcome, though another analysis makes God the subject of ‘showing him.’
rows.anchor: ( ليريه ) لام كي يكون لما آل أمره إلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza in sawʾa may be lightened.
rows.anchor: وإن خففت الهمزة قلت سوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original yā waylatī changes yāʾ to alif; al-Hasan reads the yāʾ, while alif is more eloquent because vocatives often drop yāʾ.
rows.anchor: الأصل يا ويلتي ثم أبدل من الياء ألفا

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explains vocative exclamations such as yā ʿajaban as emphatic calls for the event to appear now, stronger than merely naming its occasion.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه أن النداء إنما يقع في هذه الأشياء على المبالغة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says yā waylatā is an Arabic cry at a moment of ruin.
rows.anchor: ويا ويلتا كلمة تدعو بها العرب عند الهلاك هذا قول سيبويه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says wayl means distance.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي ويل بعد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads aʿajiztu with kasra on the jīm; the related dialect form is anomalous and distinct from the regular verb for inability.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( أعجزت ) بكسر الجيم وهذه لغة شاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-uwāri may be coordinated with akūna or parsed as the response to the question.
rows.anchor: ( فأواري ) عطف على أكون ويجوز أن يكون جواب الاستفهام

rows.speaker: يزيد بن القعقاع
rows.claim: Yazid ibn al-Qaʿqaʿ reads with kasra on the nūn and drops the hamza, following a dialect that lightens hamza in ajl; ajalta means to reap something.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يزيد بن القعقاع 32 بكسر النون وإسقاط الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Annahu is accusative with implied bi and its hāʾ refers to the matter; inna with kasra is also possible as quotation and a sentence predicate.
rows.anchor: ( أنه ) في موضع نصب أي بأنه والهاء كناية عن الحديث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan’s reading means ‘or an act of corruption’; it may instead be a verbal noun, ‘or corrupting.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( أو فسادا ) أي أو عمل فسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poetic line illustrates coordination on the accusative, describing a husband returning from war with sword and spear.
rows.anchor: ورأيت زوجك في الوغا … متقلدا سيفا ورمحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous line gives another example of coordination on the fatḥa.
rows.anchor: للبس عباءة وتقر عيني … أحب إلي من لبس الشفوف

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans read ‘and the believers say’ in the nominative, detached from the preceding clause; it can relate to their saying ‘they are with you’ or to the oath.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ( ويقول الذين آمنوا ) بالرفع على القطع من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became losers of the reward.
rows.anchor: ( فأصبحوا خاسرين ) أي خاسرين للثواب

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة وأهل الشام
rows.claim: Medina and Syria have the first cited reading; Kufans and Basrans read the dāl with fatḥa to separate two quiescent consonants, though kasra is possible and fatḥa lighter.
rows.anchor: 54 هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأهل الشام وقرأ أهل الكوفة وأهل البصرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The Kufans explain fatḥa by analogy with raddan and the opened past form; al-Farrāʾ considers yartadid better because the second radical is quiescent.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون فتح لأنه بني على التشبيه من قولك ردا

words: فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause ‘whom He loves and who love Him’ modifies qawm.
rows.anchor: ( فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه ) في موضع النعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are gentle and merciful toward believers; the phrase may be an adjective or an accusative circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: ( أذلة على المؤمنين ) نعت أي يرؤفون بهم ويرحمونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are stern toward and opposed to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ( أعزة على الكافرين ) يغلظون عليهم ويعادونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This description supports the imamate of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, who fought for God during the Prophet’s life and after his death.
rows.anchor: فدل بهذا على تثبيت إمامة أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي رضي الله عنهم

words: ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a subject-predicate sentence; God is abundant in grace and knows the interests of His creatures.
rows.anchor: ( ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء ) ابتداء وخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is nominal; the Messenger and believers are coordinated with God, and the following relative clause describes the believers.
rows.anchor: ابتداء وخبر ( ورسوله ) عطف ( والذين آمنوا ) كذلك

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Asked whether the verse means Ali ibn Abi Talib, Muhammad ibn Ali answered that Ali is a believer and took it to include all believers.
rows.anchor: أن محمد بن علي أبا جعفر سئل عن معنى إنما وليكم

words: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar holds that the plural means all believers and their mutual alliance, not imamate; its wording and operation during the Prophet’s lifetime support this.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول بين لأن الذين لجماعة المؤمنين وهذا في تولي المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at the right times with all its requirements, as one says someone carries out his work.
rows.anchor: ومعنى يقيمون الصلاة يأتون بها في أوقاتها بجميع حقوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective may also be accusative as a circumstantial expression; the scripture was sent to warn the center of the towns.
rows.anchor: نعت ويجوز نصبه في غير القرآن على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening phrase is genitive in its syntactic position; the answer to ‘if you could see’ is omitted, meaning you would see a terrible punishment.
rows.anchor: في موضع خفض أي ومن أظلم ممن قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is subject-predicate; the nūn is omitted in the possessive construction. ‘Bring yourselves out’ implies ‘free yourselves from punishment.’
rows.anchor: ( والملائكة باسطو أيديهم ) ابتداء وخبر والأصل باسطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāb al-hūn means humiliating punishment; their false claims include associating partners with God and denying Muhammad’s mission.
rows.anchor: ( اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون ) أي عذاب الهوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furādā is a circumstantial accusative and is indeclinable because it ends in the feminine alif.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال ولم ينصرف لأن فيه ألف تأنيث

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads furādan with tanwīn; Harun identifies it as Tamimi, while other dialect reports include furād with or without tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ( فرادا ) بالتنوين قال هارون لغة تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People come to God alone, without the allies who shared their error to help them.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر المعنى ولقد جئتمونا منفردين ليس معكم ناصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three explanations are offered: people are alone as at first creation, naked, or restored as they were first created.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال يكون منفردين كما خلقوا ويكون عراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged intercessors are those worshipped as partners and assigned a share of people’s wealth.
rows.anchor: أي الذين عبدتموهم وجعلتموهم شركاء في أموالكم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr takes the phrase to mean that the bond between them has been severed; baynakum is adverbial.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو أي وصلكم و ( بينكم ) على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits dead seeds and grain to produce green growth, then produces dead seeds from green growth, illustrating life from death and death from life.
rows.anchor: أي يشق النواة الميتة فيخرج منها ورقا أخضر وكذا الحبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the living human as coming from dead semen and semen as coming from a living human.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس يخرج البشر الحي من النطفة الميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given visible evidence of God’s power, the question asks how people can be turned away from truth.
rows.anchor: فمن أين تصرفون عن الحق مع ما ترون من قدرة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāliq is definite and adjectival; all grammarians except al-Kisai reject tanwīn here.
rows.anchor: نعت وهو معرفة لا يجوز فيه التنوين عند أحد من النحويين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ means the one who splits open dawn; Arabic also calls dawn falaq al-ṣubḥ and farq al-ṣubḥ.
rows.anchor: ومعنى فالق الإصباح الذي خلق له فلقا وهو الفجر

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read al-aṣbāḥ with fatḥa on the hamza, treating it as a plural of ṣubḥ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر ( فالق الأصباح ) بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash transmits from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi a reading with falaq rather than fāliq and a kasra on the hamza.
rows.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن إبراهيم النخعي أنه قرأ ( فلق الإصباح )

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use jaʿala, ‘He made the night a resting place’; Medina reads jāʿil, ‘maker of the night.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر وحمزة والكسائي ( وجعل الليل سكنا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are accusative by coordination with the implied object of jaʿala; genitive coordination is weak because its governor is weak and the elements are separated.
rows.anchor: نصب الشمس والقمر عطفا على المعنى أي وجعل والخفض بعيد

rows.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب السكوني
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Qutayb al-Sakuni reads the sun and moon in the genitive, coordinated by form with jāʿil.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ يزيد بن قطيب السكوني ( وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر )

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says ḥusbānan means ‘by calculation’ and is a plural like shihāb and shuhbān.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش حسبانا أي بحسبان قال وهو جمع حساب

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqub analyzes ḥusbān as a verbal noun of ḥasiba; ḥisāb is the noun for calculation.
rows.anchor: وقال يعقوب حسبان مصدر حسبت الشيء أحسبه حسبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the sun and moon follow measured courses that neither increase nor diminish, demonstrating God’s power and oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره جعل الله جل وعز سير الشمس والقمر بحساب لا يزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase is a subject-predicate sentence.
rows.anchor: ( ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم ) ابتداء وخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied preposition is ‘on’ or ‘in’ your path; religion is called a path because it leads to salvation.
rows.anchor: والتقدير على صراطك وفي صراطك وسمي الدين صراطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed line uses yaʿsilu and compares movement along a road to a fox; the excerpt gives no poet’s name or fuller gloss.
rows.anchor: ( لدن بهز الكف يعسل متنه … فيه كما عسل الطريق الثعلب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt marks ‘in error’ as the best reported explanation for the verse’s meaning, though the surrounding wording is fragmentary.
rows.anchor: وأحسن ما قيل في معنى 17 في الضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is parsed circumstantially.
rows.anchor: 18 على الحال وقرأ عاصم من رواية أبي بكر

rows.speaker: عاصم من رواية أبي بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Asim through Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash reads the lām with kasra; some grammarians reject it, though it can mean ‘because of your followers.’
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم من رواية أبي بكر بن عياش ( لمن تبعك ) بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is ‘destruction awaits those of them who follow you.’
rows.anchor: وقد يكون المعنى الدحر لمن تبعك منهم قال أبو إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq reads the fatḥa form as an oath lām preparing for la-amlaʾanna.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق من قرأ لمن تبعك بفتح اللام فهي عنده لام قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammarian treats the first lām as emphasis and the second as oath; the first can be dropped outside the Quran, while the second cannot, and the construction carries a conditional sense.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره لمن تبعك هي لام توكيد لأملأن لام قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is a prohibition, and ‘then you will be among the wrongdoers’ is its coordinated consequence.
rows.anchor: 19 نهى ( فتكونا من الظالمين ) جواب ويكون عطف

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains lahumā as referring to Adam and his wife.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش 20 أي إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb may appear in non-Quranic usage as ūri, like uqqitat.
rows.anchor: ( ما ووري ) ويجوز في غير القرآن أوري مثل أقتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malakayni is the predicate of takūnā; an means ‘for fear of’ or ‘to avoid,’ while Kufans explain it as ‘lest.’
rows.anchor: ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) خبر تكونا و ( أن ) في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and al-Dahhak read malikeen with kasra on the lām, meaning two kings rather than two angels.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن أبي كثير والضحاك ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd calls the variant supported by the line ‘a kingdom that does not perish’; Abu Jaʿfar calls it anomalous and rejects this argument.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيد أن احتجاج يحيى بن أبي كثير بقوله وملك لا يبلى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says Adam could not imagine reaching a station above Paradise’s angels; the line instead means permanence in the kingdom of Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ( إلا أن تكونا ملكين ) قراءة شاذة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says angels are favored with forms, wings, and honor; another view says their superiority lies in obedience and avoiding sin.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن فضل الله عز وجل الملائكة بالصور والأجنحة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address uses a construct form of the vocative.
rows.anchor: نداء مضاف ( لا يفتننكم الشيطان ) نهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is figurative like ‘do not die except as Muslims’: remain Muslim until death comes.
rows.anchor: ( لا يفتننكم الشيطان ) نهي وهو مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kamā is an adjective for an implied verbal noun; the entry discusses forms for father and mother and vocatives such as yā abata.
rows.anchor: ( كما ) بفي موضع نصب نعت لمصدر ( أخرج أبويكم من الجنة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be circumstantial or a new sentence; li-yuriyahumā is purposive.
rows.anchor: ( ينزع عنهما لباسهما ) في موضع نصب على الحال ويكون مستأنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yuriyahumā expresses purpose.
rows.anchor: ( ليريهما ) نصب بلام كي ( إنه يراكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original yarʾākum had a hamza that was lightened; huwa wa-qabīluhu coordinates with and emphasizes the hidden subject, unlike coordination with an overt noun.
rows.anchor: ( إنه يراكم ) الأصل يرأاكم ثم خففت الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says jinn are seen only in a prophet’s time as a sign of prophethood, since their created form is invisible and they are seen when transformed.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن قوله إنه يراكم هو وقبيله من حيث لا ترونهم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq explains ḥaythu as built because it names no specific location and its following clause is a complement; Kufans also report kasra and annexation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هي مبنية لعلتين إحداهما أنها لا تدل على موضع بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement describes devils as allies of those who do not believe.
rows.anchor: ( إنا جعلنا الشياطين أولياء للذين لا يؤمنون ) أي وصفناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is accusative as comparison: people return as God first created them; Abu Ishaq attaches it to the preceding phrase about emerging from the earth.
rows.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب أي تعودون كما بدأكم أي كما خلقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first farīqan is accusative with hadā; the second follows an implied verb, ‘and He led another group astray.’
rows.anchor: نصب بهدى ( وفريقا ) نصب بإضمار فعل أي وأضل فريقا

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisai and al-Farrāʾ instead parse the return as two groups, one guided and one condemned to error; Abu’s reading explicitly says ‘you return as two groups.’
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء التقدير يعودون فريقا هدى وفريقا

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads annahum with fatḥa, meaning ‘because they.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر ( أنهم ) بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are better than powerless idols, so the question asks how they can find or call on them.
rows.anchor: أي أنتم أفضل منهم فكيف تجدونهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read ayd as a dialect form; the author notes that hand, foot, and ear are feminine and take feminine hāʾ in diminutives, while yad restores a yāʾ in its diminutive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ( أم لهم أيد يبطشون ) وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are those associated with God and assigned a portion of people’s wealth.
rows.anchor: ( قل ادعوا شركاءكم ) أي الذين شركتموهم فجعلتم لهم قسطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original kīdūnī loses its yāʾ, with kasra signaling the omitted letter; likewise fa-lā tunẓirūn means ‘do not delay me.’
rows.anchor: ( ثم كيدون ) والأصل كيدوني بالياء حذفت الياء

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: Asim al-Jahdari reads ‘my protector is God, who sent down the Book,’ identifying the protector as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الجحدري ( إن ولي الله الذي نزل الكتاب ) يعني جبرئيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī here means God as guardian and helper; the walī of a thing protects it and prevents harm.
rows.anchor: ومعنى وليي الله حافظي وناصري الله وولي الشيء الذي يحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction has a subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ والخبر ( لا يستطيعون نصركم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is conditional, so the nūn is dropped; lā yasmaʿū is its response. Wa-tarāhum starts a new clause, yanẓurūna ilayka is circumstantial, and looking means opening the eyes rather than seeing.
rows.anchor: شرط فلذلك حذفت منه النون والجواب ( لا يسمعوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun appears in the predicate because the statement follows a verb used of rational beings.
rows.anchor: وخبر عنهم بالواو لأن الخبر جرى على فعل من يعقل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله إبراهيم بن محمد
rows.claim: Abu Abdallah Ibrahim ibn Muhammad says al-ʿafw is charity, a small amount from much.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله إبراهيم بن محمد العفو الزكاة لأنها يسير

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar derives al-ʿafw from something worn away; ‘take the easy portion’ means do not press people and treat them leniently.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهو من عفا إذا درس وقد يقال خذ العفو منه

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads al-ʿurf as al-maʿrūf, what reason recognizes as good.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر ( بالعرف ) أي المعروف ومعنى المعروف ما كان حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After presenting proof and commanding right conduct, turn away from ignorant abuse to preserve dignity rather than answer in kind.
rows.anchor: أي إذا أقمت عليهم الحجة وأمرتهم بالمعروف فجهلوا عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh is Satan’s prompting toward what is forbidden, especially in anger; seek God’s refuge, for He hears the appeal and knows what is needed.
rows.anchor: نزغ أي إن وسوس إليك الشيطان عند الغضب بما لا يحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanzaghannaka is jussive under the condition and emphatic with nūn; Sibawayh cites Arabic usage with the same emphasis.
rows.anchor: ( ينزغنك ) في موضع جزم بالشرط وكد بالنون وحسن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious avoid sins; when Satan touches them, they reflect on God’s power and favors, leave the sin, and regain clear sight.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إن الذين اتقوا المعاصي إذا لحقهم شيء من الشيطان

rows.speaker: أهل البصرة وأهل مكة
rows.claim: Basrans and Meccans use ṭaʾif; Medina and Kufa read ṭāʾif, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr is reported to read ṭayf with doubled yāʾ.
rows.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل البصرة وأهل مكة وقرأ أهل المدينة وأهل الكوفة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The normal Arabic form is ṭayf without a doubled yāʾ, from ṭāfa yaṭīfu; al-Kisai calls it shortened, meaning a thought in the heart or a dream image like ṭāʾif.
rows.anchor: كلام العرب في مثل هذا طيف بالتخفيف على أنه مصدر

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim says al-Asmaʿi denied verbal nouns on the fīʿl pattern; Abu Jaʿfar answers that this is not a verbal noun but can mean ṭāʾif.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم سألت الأصمعي عن طيف فقال ليس في المصادر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is reported to read tadhakkarū with a doubled dhāl, which Abu Jaʿfar says has no grammatical basis.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد ( تذكروا ) بتشديد الذال ولا وجه له في العربية
